Every construction is a pure function of checked tables, so the `Machine` proofs\nand the Definition ID scheme carry over, and no behavior is defined outside a step function an\nauthor wrote (AUT-07a, AUT-09). The word is `compose`, not `system`: `system` is the reserved party\nfor the implementation under test (glossary Party) and the elaborator enforces it.\n\nVersion one composes only for `verify` Queries. No functional, canary, or exploratory set runs over\na composed Model, so the Producer, the realizations, Case production, Testpilot, every Case fixture,\nthe production canary's pinned Case identity, the recorded control Run, the exploration coverage\ngolden, and the replay bridge are unchanged: every committed fixture and golden is byte-identical\nafter this spec. The caller module stays where it is, and so do the Start and Outage entities: moving\nthe `operation` entity would rewrite every `temporal.nexus.caller.*` ID and re-pin the canary, and a\nshared `workflow` entity needs a key decision the grammar cannot express today (Start correlates by\n`firstExecutionRunId`, Outage by `workflowTaskCompletedEventId` because its only evidence carries no\nrun id). Both are recorded under Boundaries as the follow-up. Rule text that needs a\nGOV-02 draft is listed in Decision Context. The direction note `.plans/UMPIRE4_DIRECTION.md` and the\nconversation of 2026-09-26 record the reasoning.\n\n## Overview\n\nToday `Temporal.Feature` holds seven machines shaped around the upstream tests they replace, three\nof them copies of the Nexus reply logic, and no Property can relate a workflow to the worker that\nserves it or an operation to the worker that answers it. This spec gives the model a way to compose\nentities into one Model for cross-entity claims, adds the first entity module, and removes one of the\nthree copies. The full unification, which moves the operation entity, re-pins the canary, and needs\nan entity key that varies by use case, is named as the follow-up.\n\n## Goal & Context\n<!-- scope: business -->\n\nThe vision's first line is one model for software behavior. The tree has seven: `Workflow/Start` and\n`Workflow/Outage` each declare `entity workflow` with a different key and their own `startWorkflow`;\n`Nexus/Pair` and `Nexus/Control` copy the caller's reply logic over new phase enums; `System/Info`\nhas an `entity server` nothing else mentions. Only `Nexus/Caller` has the intended shape.\n\nThree structural causes: a machine tracks one entity and nothing composes machines of different\nentities; the search enumerates paths, so a composed state space was unaffordable before fn-88; and\nthe Case pipeline made the upstream test the unit of authoring. The concrete symptom this spec fixes\nfirst: `workerStop` is a stutter row on the operation machine, so the schedule-to-start timeout\nScenario orders the stop before the request by convention. With a worker machine composed in,\n`handlerReply` is enabled only while the worker polls, and that ordering becomes a checked fact.\n\nWho benefits: an author writing a cross-entity claim has a Model to write it against; the worker\nbecomes a first-class entity instead of a stutter row on two other machines; the Control model\nbecomes a visible one-row delta on the Pair machine instead of a third copy.\n\n## Architecture & Data Models\n<!-- scope: technical -->\n\n```text\nTemporal/Feature/\n  Worker/Model.lean        entity worker (key taskQueue), workerStop, workerResume, serve,\n                           machine polling                                                     new\n  Workflow/Outage/Model.lean unchanged; gains compose workerOutage (outage machine ∥ worker) and a\n                           cross-entity verify Query beside its functional set\n  Nexus/Caller/Model.lean  unchanged; gains machine handlerWorker (from: polling restrict:), compose\n                           nexusCaller (nexusProtocol ∥ handlerWorker), and a cross-entity verify\n                           Query beside the existing sets\n  Nexus/Control/Model.lean machine nexusControl from: pair extend: …, byte-identical Case        rewritten\n  Nexus/Pair, Nexus/Success, Workflow/Start, System/Info                                        unchanged\n```\n\nConstructions, all in `Umpire.Command`, all pure functions of checked tables:\n\n- **`compose` command.** Keys: `for:` the entities tracked; `state:` an author-written `structure`\n  with one field per member (field names are what predicates read; the structure derives no\n  `Finite`); `members:` one `field: machine` line per member;\n  `sync:` one line per synchronized action, `name: field.action ∥ field.action …`, naming which\n  member's action each participant is, first-named member's outcome reported; `starts:` and\n  `ends:` over the composed state, since members like the worker have no natural end. The command\n  generates `<name>.Action`, `<name>.Outcome`, and `<name>.Fact` as tagged unions with one\n  constructor per member wrapping that member's type, so catalog keys never collide and predicates\n  write `step.facts.contains (.operation .nexusOperationCompleted)`. Catalog keys obey\n  `FiniteCatalog.validKey` (alphanumerics, `-`, `_`), so an unsynchronized action is keyed\n  `<field>_<member key>` and a composed state `_`-joins its members' state keys in field order, the\n  spelling `instances:` already uses for `1_accepted` and its product states; a member field name\n  containing `_` is a located error. A synchronized action is keyed by its `sync:` name. Authors\n  refer to members with dots, `operation.handlerReply (async)`, and Scenario `actions:`, Scenario\n  `starts:`, and Property `when:` resolve those references and `sync:` names to the catalog keys,\n  so the elaborator's last-component action lookup and `-`-split phase lookup are extended for\n  compositions.\n  Semantics: an unsynchronized action steps its owner and leaves the others unchanged; a\n  synchronized step is enabled only when every participant has a row from its current state, and\n  its results are the ordered product of the participants' results, sorted by the existing step\n  order key, refused above 16 results with the counts; a participant may own a classless action\n  synchronized with a classed one, in which case its row applies to every class; two members\n  owning an action of the same name that no `sync:` line names is a located error; timers never\n  synchronize and are keyed per member.\n- **Reachable enumeration.** The composed table is built by a frontier breadth-first walk from the\n  composed start states through the members' tables, evaluated at elaboration and emitted as a\n  literal table. The state catalog is the reachable set sorted by lowered order key, as `instances:`\n  orders its catalogs, so the fingerprint is independent of discovery and member order. The bound\n  check is reachable states times actions against `enumerationBound`. An action never jointly\n  enabled is dropped from the catalog with a located warning. This walk is the command's own; the\n  literal is sorted by a total key before emission, since a stable sort would let ties carry the\n  `members:` order into the fingerprint.\n- **Composed state fields, starts, ends, timers.** The composed Model lowers every member's state\n  fields as its own state fields keyed `<field>_<memberField>` (a one-field member as `<field>`);\n  the member field itself is not a state field, because a whole-structure spelling would make every\n  nested predicate a disjunction the clause language refuses.\n- **Field-addressed requirements.** The `property` command's predicate enumeration fixes whole\n  states, outcomes, and facts today, so a claim on one member's field, `step.state.worker.phase ==\n  .polling` while the other member varies, fixes nothing and is refused. This spec adds one\n  requirement kind: a state field is fixed when every accepted step carries that field's value and\n  changing it to any other value of that field's catalog is rejected; it lowers to the same\n  transition-contract clause on the field's model value, which both the reference evaluator and the\n  Property monitors already match, because each offers a state's fields beside the state to a\n  resulting-state pattern. A claim that names every field of a unique composed state, as the\n  Outage claim can, is carried as a whole-state requirement without it. `starts:` and `ends:` on\n  `compose` name member-qualified values (`workflow.completed`); a composed state is terminal when\n  the named member field holds a listed value, and the machine rule that `ends:` values share one\n  carrying field does not apply. Each member's `timers:`, `unobservable:` entries, and `evidence:`\n  lines are lifted under `<field>.` keys; a `sync:` line naming a timer is a located error. A member\n  may itself refine another machine; the composition carries neither `refines:` nor an abstract\n  field.\n- **Search backend.** fn-88 is a dependency and closes before this spec starts: `Selection.select`\n  chooses the backend per Query with no author-facing override, `veil` when the Property lowers to\n  monitors and the Scenario is pinned, `reference` otherwise with a recorded reason, and\n  `Selection.cutover` is true. The two shipped claims are same-step `when:` Properties with a\n  state-field requirement over a `scenario` declaration, which lowers, so each runs on `veil` with\n  reason `default`; the kernel replay gate runs on every result as it does for every Query. The\n  backend differential is registry-driven and covers a Query once the module declaring it is\n  imported by the sweep module and its expected line is pinned, so every Query this spec declares,\n  fixture or shipped, is listed there.\n- **Proofs.** A generic theorem shows that a decidable check, `composedTableAgrees members literal\n  = true`, implies soundness and completeness of the literal with respect to the composition\n  function over reachable sources. The `compose` command emits that check for each composition by\n  `decide +kernel`, as the refinement decision does today, and refuses the composition with a located\n  error when it fails. The kernel time of that check and of the law proof is measured on both\n  shipped compositions, beside the predicate-enumeration seconds of their Properties. If either\n  exceeds the elaboration budget, the first fallback is a proof-shape change (per-row lemma\n  batching, `Nat` constructor-index comparisons instead of `String` equality inside the decided\n  `Bool`); `native_decide` comes only with the explicit policy approval `LEAN_GUIDELINES.md` §5\n  requires, recorded per module, and on Lean 4.32 it mints a per-call axiom rather than\n  `Lean.ofReduceBool`, so the R5 axiom pin fails on it by construction. `compose` elaborates to\n  `Umpire.Command.DeclaredModel` as `machine` does; a Query's `check` over it yields\n  `Umpire.Command.CheckedModel`, which still carries a `realizable` field as it does for every\n  `verify` Query, and nothing reads it because no set names a composition.\n- **`restrict:` and `extend:` on `machine`.** `machine x from: source restrict: [actions]` keeps only\n  the listed actions' rows and drops the rest from the catalog; `evidence:` lines for facts no\n  remaining row returns, `timers:` and `unobservable:` entries without rows are filtered. `extend:\n  action: step` appends the author's results to the named action's rows, with a located error for a\n  result at a source state where the action has no row and for a duplicate result; results are\n  sorted by the step order key. Both keys may appear on one machine; `restrict:` applies first. A\n  derived machine inherits neither `refines:` nor the abstract state field. `Nexus/Control` becomes\n  `from: pair extend: handlerReply: forgedStep` with the machine name, catalog keys, and result order\n  it has today, so its Case fixture and the recorded control Run under `tools/umpire/replay/testdata`\n  stay byte-identical; a derived machine re-owns its catalogs under its own namespace.\n- **Entity module.** `Worker/Model.lean` declares `entity worker` keyed by task queue, with\n  `workerStop`, `workerResume`, a classless `serve` action (a polling worker serves; a stopped one\n  has no row), and machine `polling` with `starts: [polling]` and `ends: [polling, stopped]`. The\n  handler's task-queue worker and the workflow's task-queue worker are two instances of this entity,\n  named by the member field of the composition that uses them. The caller and Outage modules keep\n  their own `workerStop` actions in version one; the compositions synchronize with them by name.\n- **Two compositions.** `workerOutage` composes `workflowOutage ∥ worker` with `sync: workerStop:\n  workflow.workerStop ∥ worker.workerStop`, `workerResume` likewise, and `awaitCompletion:\n  workflow.awaitCompletion ∥ worker.serve`, and verifies that a stopped worker completes no\n  workflow, as a claim on the unique composed state a completion leaves. `nexusCaller` composes\n  `operation ∥ handlerWorker`, where `handlerWorker` is `from: polling restrict: [workerStop,\n  serve]` declared in the caller module, with `sync: workerStop: operation.workerStop ∥\n  worker.workerStop` and `handlerReply: operation.handlerReply ∥ worker.serve`, and verifies with a\n  bare `when: handlerReply`, which covers every reply class, and a field-addressed requirement that\n  `handlerReply` never fires while the worker is stopped. The restriction is what keeps\n  `workerResume` out of that composition; composing the full `polling` machine would admit a\n  stop-resume-reply path the boundary excludes. The Outage functional set and the seven caller\n  Queries keep their machines.\n- **Lint.** `make lint-model` gains `feature-entity-uniqueness`: under `Temporal.Feature` production\n  modules, an `entity` or `action` name declared twice is a violation unless allowlisted; the initial\n  allowlist records the duplicates that exist once the worker module lands (`workflow` in Caller,\n  Start, and Outage; `startWorkflow` in Start and Outage; `workerStop` in Caller, Outage, and Worker;\n  `workerResume` in Outage and Worker) each with the follow-up spec that removes it, test and\n  specimen modules are excluded, and the diagnostic names both modules. Any other duplicate fails. It reads `Registry.entities` in the environment-importing driver, since the\n  import-graph rules cannot see declarations.\n\n## API Contracts\n<!-- scope: technical -->\n\n- `compose` produces an `Umpire.Command.DeclaredModel`; `property`, `scenario`, `limits`, and\n  `query` accept it as they accept a machine, and a Query's `check` yields\n  `Umpire.Command.CheckedModel`. The `machine` command declares one over a\n   `structure` of finite fields with one step function per action, naming the entity it tracks, the\n   phases it starts and ends in, its timers, its setup parameters and the observation confirming\n   each Fact; `Umpire.Command.MachineDeclaration` is its record.\n+  *Amendment (drafted by fn-92; awaiting GOV-02 approval.)* A machine may instead be derived from\n+  another: `from:` names the source, `restrict:` keeps the listed actions' rows and drops the rest,\n+  and `extend:` adds the author's results to an action's rows, in the step order\n+  (`Umpire.Command.Derived`). A derived machine keeps its source's entity, state type, starts, ends\n+  and setup, and the evidence of every fact its rows still record; it reaches its rows through the\n+  source's own step functions, owns its Action catalog and Definition IDs, and inherits neither\n+  `refines:` nor the source's abstract state field.\n - **Entity (`Umpire.Command.Entity`).** Something with identity that a machine keeps state for,\n   declared by the `entity` command with the entities it refers to and the key recorded data names\n   an instance by. A Scenario runs over a number of `instances:` of it. State belongs to machines,\n   not entities: two machines may track one entity differently.\n - **Party.** Who performs an action: a name a Model declares by using it on an `action`. `system`\n   is reserved for the implementation under test, performs no declared action, and owns the\n   timers. A set binds every other party; a fault is an ordinary action of the party that causes\n   it.\n+  *Amendment (drafted by fn-92; awaiting GOV-02 approval.)* The command that builds one Model from\n+  several machines is `compose`, not `system`: `system` is this reserved party, and a composition is\n+  no party. It declares no action; each of its actions is one or more of its members' actions,\n+  performed by their parties.\n - **Refinement (`Umpire.Command.Refinement`).** A machine that `refines:` another through a state\n   `map:`: a stuttering forward simulation the `machine` command decides over the two tables, so\n   every Property declared on the abstract machine is read on the refining machine's paths. It is\n   not an Implementation Link, which SEM-08 reserves for the connection from `Temporal.Feature` to\n   `Temporal.System`; both machines of a refinement are product behavior.\n+  *Amendment (drafted by fn-92; awaiting GOV-02 approval.)* A composition does not refine and\n+  carries no `refines:` or abstract field, though a member may itself be a refining machine; a\n+  derived machine does not inherit its source's refinement.\n+- **Composition (`Umpire.Command.Compose`).** *(drafted by fn-92; awaiting GOV-02 approval.)* One\n+  Model built by the `compose` command from machines of different entities, for a claim no one of\n+  them can state. Requesting an\n   Action neither chooses its Model Outcome nor proves that the Action occurred at runtime. The\n   `action` command declares one with its party, the entity it creates or acts on, typed inputs\n   over `enum` domains and an optional protobuf schema (`Umpire.Command.Action`). Each member of an\n   input domain is a class, and a constructor with finite fields is one class per assignment of\n   them; a Scenario selects classes, and a machine's step function is written over them.\n - **Model Outcome.** The result the Model produces for an Action. It is an expected model result,\n   not a runtime result.\n - **Step (`Umpire.Step`).** One model step and what it produced: an `outcome`, a `state`, and a list\n   of `facts`.\n - **Fact.** A claim the Model makes at a Step, such as “the Nexus operation received a\n   cancellation.” Logs, spans, RPCs, and records are Evidence used to decide whether the claim held\n   during a Run. Concepts\n \n ### 2.1 Entity\n \n An entity is a kind of thing with identity. It declares what it refers to and the key recorded data\n uses to name an instance. It declares no state: state belongs to the machines that track the entity\n (section 2.3), so two machines can describe the same entity at different detail.\n \n ```lean\n entity workflow\n \n entity operation\n   refer:\n     caller: workflow\n   key: scheduledEvent\n ```\n \n A Model holds several instances of each entity, bounded by Limits. References are compared, never\n interpreted; the realization binds them to runtime identifiers. Several instances are what\n `TestNexusAsyncOperationWithMultipleCallers` needs (five operations sharing one handler workflow).\n \n > Amended during fn-85 `.4`, 2026-09-19. Instances are declared where a Scenario runs over them:\n > `instances: 2` on the `scenario`, with each action naming the instance that takes it\n > (`awaitStart 2`). Decisions\n \n Recorded 2026-09-10 with the user; items marked *revised* changed in the simplification pass, and\n fn-85 delivered them as revised. Where delivery departed from a decision, the dated `.N` amendment\n under the section it concerns says how.\n \n 1. **A party is fixed on the action; a set binds it.** *Revised:* the bindings are `driven` and\n    `observed` (previously `test` and `environment`, which collided with a party named\n    `environment`), and `system` is the only reserved party. Timers are `system` behavior written as\n    `after(<timer>)` in rows; faults are actions of a declared party.\n 2. **The author claims classes; exploration owns the evidence.** A class is an enum constructor.\n    Single-value classes need no evidence; a multi-value class is a claim recorded in Provenance with\n    its example (*revised* word, previously \"representative\"), and exploration tries its other\n    members.\n 3. **Protobuf descriptors stay Umpire's only schema.** *Revised:* actions have no `kind`. Whether an\n    action is a call, a command or a reply changed nothing the verifier does, so the distinction stays\n    in the realization, where `Umpire.Operation`'s `unaryRpc` and `sdkCommand` live on. `event`\n    becomes the observation catalog. The schema line is optional.\n 4. **One machine by default; a product machine when needed.** A protocol machine `refines:` a\n    product machine through a state `map:` that defaults by name; steps are derived. It is a\n    refinement, not an Implementation Link.\n+   *Amended during fn-92, 2026-09-29:* machines of different entities compose instead: `compose`\n+   pairs their actions with `sync:` lines into one Model for a cross-entity claim, and a machine\n+   that differs from another by rows is derived with `from:` plus `restrict:` or `extend:` rather\n+   than copied, as the negative control is.\n 5. **One Model for HSM and CHASM, run under both.** Deliberate config-controlled differences are\n    setup parameters; the rollout switch is a set's `repeat`; storage layout is a white-box Known Gap.\n 6. **Words.** `action`, `observation`, `machine`, `refines`, `examples`, `driven`, `observed`.\n    `interface` was rejected as a method-set contract type duplicating Action; `model` and\n    `statemachine` because Model is the checked behavior and Machine the glossary's transition\n    relation; \"mechanism machine\" because MOD-02 gives implementation mechanisms to\n    `Temporal.System`; a top-level `link` because SEM-08 reserves Implementation Link.\n 7. *New:* **State belongs to machines, not entities.** An entity declares identity, references and a\n    key; each machine declares the state it keeps, so the product and protocol machines can track the\n    same entity differently.\n 8. *New:* **Event observations are not declared.** Evidence names resolve against the realization's\n    catalog; only derived observations such as reads are declared.\n 9. *New:* **Validation is rows, not a separate `rules:` block.** Rejections are the first rows of a\n    machine, using the existing first-match order. Constant entity traits (`vary:`) are setup\n    parameters. A machine names its `ends:`, which rows and Properties read as `terminal`.\n 10. *New, needs a rule amendment:* **The realization lives in `Temporal.Case`**, beside the templates\n     it replaces, because MOD-10 forbids `Temporal.System` from importing Feature machines; MOD-02\n     lists Evidence mappings under `Temporal.System` and needs amending to allow it.\n 11. *New:* **Worker instructions carry API messages.** A workflow command carries its\n     `temporal.api.command.v1` attributes and a handler reply its `temporal.api.nexus.v1` message, so\n     the action's schema and its instruction are the same type and no Testpilot field is added per\n     server option. SDK-only options go in an extension field beside the message.\n \n ## Appendix A. A composition over the operation and its worker\n\nA `compose` block builds one Model from machines of different entities, for a claim no one of them\ncan state. The protocol machine cannot see the handler's worker: its `workerStop` is a stutter row.\nComposed with the worker entity's machine, restricted by `restrict:` to the actions the caller's\nview needs, each `sync:` line makes one step of both members, so a reply is enabled only where the\nworker's `serve` has a row, which is only while it polls. The composed state is an author-written\nstructure with one field per member, and a Property reads one member's field while the other\nvaries. Scenario and Property names resolve member-qualified actions (`operation.schedule`) and\n`sync:` names (`handlerReply`); no set names a composition, so its Query is a `verify` Query.\n\n<!-- authoring: composition -->\n```lean\n/-! ### The operation and the handler's worker\n\nThe protocol machine's worker stop is a stutter row: the operation cannot see its handler's worker,\nso the schedule-to-start Scenario orders the stop before the request by convention. Composed with\nthe worker of the handler's task queue, the stop is the worker's own phase change and every reply\nis the worker serving, so a reply has a row only while the worker polls. No set names the\ncomposition; it is what the cross-entity claim is verified over. -/\n\n/-- The caller's view of the handler's worker: it stops and it serves. The worker entity, a second composition, and a derived machine\n\nSection 12's composition names the worker entity's module. This section quotes that module, the\nOutage Model's composition and the derived negative control, and the drift test checks their marked\nregions as it checks this file's: a region name is unique across every file the walkthrough quotes,\nand each file closes its last quoted region with its own `-- authoring: end`.\n\n**An entity module.** [`Temporal/Feature/Worker/Model.lean`](Temporal/Feature/Worker/Model.lean)\ndeclares one entity, the worker of a task queue, and no set, Case or Query: nothing in it is\nrealized on its own. Its machine is what a composition synchronizes with. The handler's worker and\nthe workflow's worker are two instances of it, and the composition that uses one names it by its\nmember field.\n\n<!-- authoring: worker -->\n```lean\n/-! ### Entities and domains -/\n\n/-- A worker is named by the task queue it polls: the handler's worker and the workflow's worker are\ntwo instances of this entity, told apart by their queue. -/\nentity worker\n  key: taskQueue\n\nenum Phase\n  | polling\n  | stopped\n\nstructure WorkerState where\n  phase : Phase\n  deriving BEq, DecidableEq, Repr, Finite\n\nenum WorkerOutcome\n  | accepted\n\n/-- A worker records nothing of its own: its stop and resume are faults the Run records against no\nentity, and what it serves is recorded by the work it serves. -/\ninductive WorkerFact\n  deriving BEq, DecidableEq, Repr, Finite\n\n/-! ### The actions\n\nThe two faults are the `worker` party's and name no entity, as the outage machine spells them. The\nserve action is the worker's own and takes no input, so a composition may synchronize it with an\naction of any class. -/\n\naction workerStop\n  party: worker\n\naction workerResume\n  party: worker\n\naction serve\n  party: worker\n  on: worker\n```\n\nThe machine starts polling and may end in either phase, because a worker has no natural end. A\npolling worker serves; a stopped one has no `serve` row, which is the whole point of composing it.\n\n<!-- authoring: polling -->\n```lean\n/-! ### The machine -/\n\n/-- A polling worker stops; a stopped one has nothing to stop. -/\ndef stopStep (state : WorkerState) :\n    List (Step WorkerState WorkerOutcome WorkerFact) :=\n  if state.phase != .polling then [] else\n  [{ outcome := .accepted, state := { phase := .stopped }, facts := [] }]\n\n/-- A stopped worker resumes polling; a polling one has nothing to resume. -/\ndef resumeStep (state : WorkerState) :\n    List (Step WorkerState WorkerOutcome WorkerFact) :=\n  if state.phase != .stopped then [] else\n  [{ outcome := .accepted, state := { phase := .polling }, facts := [] }]\n\n/-- A polling worker serves and keeps polling; a stopped one serves nothing. -/\ndef serveStep (state : WorkerState) :\n    List (Step WorkerState WorkerOutcome WorkerFact) :=\n  if state.phase != .polling then [] else\n  [{ outcome := .accepted, state, facts := [] }]\n\n/-- A worker has no natural end: it may be left polling or stopped. -/\nmachine polling\n  for: worker\n  state: WorkerState\n  starts: [polling]\n  ends: [polling, stopped]\n  steps:\n    workerStop: stopStep\n    workerResume: resumeStep\n    serve: serveStep\n```\n\nAn entity or action name is declared once across the production modules under\n`Temporal.Feature`: `make lint-model` fails a second declaration and names both modules\n(`feature-entity-uniqueness`, drafted as MOD-18). Its allowlist, in `model/ModelLint/Entity.lean`,\nholds the duplicates that remain once the worker module exists (`workflow` in the caller, Start and\nOutage modules, `startWorkflow` in Start and Outage, `workerStop` in the caller, Outage and worker\nmodules, `workerResume` in Outage and worker), each removed by the follow-up that lets a use case\nchoose its entity key and moves the operation entity. Test modules and the success specimen are\nout of scope.\n\n**A second composition.** The Outage Model\n([`Temporal/Feature/Workflow/Outage/Model.lean`](Temporal/Feature/Workflow/Outage/Model.lean))\ncomposes its unchanged machine with the full `polling` machine. All three worker actions are\nsynchronized: the two faults are one step of the workflow's stutter row and the worker's phase\nchange, and the wait for completion is the worker serving. The claim fixes the one composed state a\ncompletion leaves, so it holds as a whole-state requirement; the caller's claim in section 12 fixes\none member's field while the other varies, which is the field-addressed requirement.\n\n<!-- authoring: outage -->\n```lean\n/-! ### The workflow and its worker\n\nThe outage machine composed with the worker of the workflow's task queue. The two faults are one\nstep of both: the workflow's stutter row and the worker's phase change. The wait is the worker\nserving the workflow task, so it has a row only while the worker polls, and the workflow completes\nin no state where the worker is stopped. The functional set stays over the machine alone; the\ncomposition is what the cross-entity claim is verified over. -/\n\nstructure WorkerOutageState where\n  workflow : OutageState\n  worker : Worker.WorkerState\n  deriving BEq, DecidableEq, Repr\n\ncompose workerOutage\n  for: [workflow, Worker.worker]\n  state: WorkerOutageState\n  members:\n    workflow: workflowOutage\n    worker: Worker.polling\n  sync:\n    workerStop: workflow.workerStop ∥ worker.workerStop\n    workerResume: workflow.workerResume ∥ worker.workerResume\n    awaitCompletion: workflow.awaitCompletion ∥ worker.serve\n  starts: [workflow.pending, worker.polling]\n  ends: [workflow.completed]\n\n/- A completion leaves the one composed state in which the workflow is completed and its worker is\npolling, and records the completed event: no workflow completes while its worker is stopped. -/\nproperty completedByPollingWorker\n  machine: workerOutage\n  when: awaitCompletion\n  holds: fun step =>\n    step.state.workflow.phase == .completed && step.state.worker.phase == .polling &&\n      step.facts.contains (.workflow .workflowExecutionCompleted)\n\n/- The outage over the composition: the stop and the resume move the worker, and the wait is\nserved by the resumed worker. -/\nscenario outageServed\n  model: workerOutage\n  starts: workflow.pending\n  actions: [workerStop, workflow.startWorkflow, workerResume, awaitCompletion]\n\nquery stoppedWorkerCompletesNothing\n  verify: completedByPollingWorker\n  in: outageServed\n  limits: four\n```\n\nWhat `compose` generates, for both compositions:\n\n- `workerOutage.Action`, `.Outcome` and `.Fact`, tagged unions with one constructor per member\n  wrapping that member's type, which is why a predicate writes\n  `step.facts.contains (.workflow .workflowExecutionCompleted)`.\n- Catalog keys a fixture and a Definition ID can carry: a composed state `_`-joins its members'\n  state keys in field order (`completed_polling`), an unsynchronized action is `<field>_<key>`\n  (`workflow_startWorkflow`), and a synchronized action is its `sync:` name. Member timers,\n  unobservable entries and evidence lines are lifted under the same `<field>_<key>` spelling. A\n  member's state fields are lowered as `<field>_<memberField>` (`<field>` for a one-field member),\n  which is what a field-addressed requirement fixes. Definition IDs hang off the owner\n  `compose-<name>` under the file's namespace.\n- The table of reachable rows only: a breadth-first walk from the starts over the members' tables,\n  every catalog and each row's results sorted by the lowered order key, emitted as a literal. The\n  walk refuses a composition whose reachable states times actions exceed the enumeration bound,\n  with both counts. `workerOutage` reaches 6 states; `nexusCaller` reaches 316 and 1468 rows.\n- `<name>.agrees`, a theorem decided by `decide +kernel` that the literal agrees with the\n  composition of the members' tables over every state the starts reach: rows grouped by source\n  state, each member table read once. A literal the kernel refuses is a located error. On\n  `nexusCaller` the decisions take 56.5 s of kernel time and the whole caller Model file 241 s at\n  6.8 GB, which is the cost of composing a 158-state machine.\n\nA step of an unsynchronized action moves its member and leaves the others; a `sync:` step is\nenabled only where every participant has a row, and its results are the ordered product of theirs.\nTwo members owning an action of one name that no `sync:` line pairs is a located error, and so is a\n`sync:` line naming a timer. The composition carries no `refines:` and no abstract field. No set\nnames it: `set` over a composition is refused, so its Queries are `verify` Queries, and\n`Selection.select` runs both shipped ones on `veil` with reason `default`.\n\n**A derived machine.** A `machine` with `from:` takes its source's entity, state type, starts, ends,\nsetup and evidence, and its rows through the source's own step functions; it carries neither\n`refines:` nor the abstract field, and it generates its own Action catalog, so its Definition IDs\nare its own. `restrict: [actions]` keeps the listed actions' rows and drops the rest, every timer\nand unobservable entry, and every evidence line for a fact no kept row records (section 12's\n`handlerWorker`). `extend:` adds an author's results to an action's rows, sorted into the step order\nkey; a result where the source has no row, or one the source already returns, is a located error.\nBoth may appear on one machine, and `restrict:` applies first. The negative control\n([`Temporal/Feature/Nexus/Control/Model.lean`](Temporal/Feature/Nexus/Control/Model.lean)) is the\npair machine plus one forged result, so one function is its only step code, and its catalogs, its\nCase fixture and its recorded Run are the ones the copied machine had.\n\n<!-- authoring: derived -->\n```lean\n/-! ### The machine\n\nThe pair Model's machine -- the operation without its deadlines and retries -- plus the forged row.\nThe machine is derived from it rather than copied: every row is the pair machine's, and the one\nfunction written here returns the one result the platform never takes. -/\n\n/-- The forged row: the non-retryable error completes the operation and records the completed\nevent. The platform's row for that error, which fails the operation and records the failed event,\nis the pair machine's and stays beside it. -/\ndef controlForgedStep (state : PairState) (reply : Reply) :\n    List (Step PairState PairOutcome PairFact) :=\n  if state.phase != .scheduled then [] else\n  match reply with\n  | .handlerError false =>\n      [{ outcome := .accepted, state := { phase := .succeeded },\n         facts := [.nexusOperationCompleted] }]\n  | _ => []\n\nmachine nexusControl\n  from: pair\n  extend:\n    handlerReply: controlForgedStep\n```\n\n## 14.
